attribution_correction.earlier_wrong_claim: An earlier integration draft attributed this fixture to freeenergylab/amber_tutorials (MDforIL2/1PY2). That repository contains an IL2 + SP4206 system, not this T4 lysozyme + catechol system, and has no 1XEP preparation. The claim was rejected.
attribution_correction.verification: The fixture protein heavy atoms are bit-identical to 1XEP chain A (1290/1290, max 0.000 A); the UNL catechol matches 1XEP CAQ altloc A within 0.0133 A after ring-order mapping.

config0_reference.protocol: OpenMM AmberPrmtopFile.createSystem(nonbondedMethod=NoCutoff, constraints=None, rigidWater=False, removeCMMotion=False); force group 0 = bonded, 1 = NonbondedForce/CustomNonbondedForce; dispersion correction off; Platform CPU, Threads=1, DeterministicForces=true; config 0 = source coordinates; configs 1,2 apply the INTERFACE.md 0.02*config nm sine perturbation
config0_reference.verification: A fresh OpenMM 8.6.1 recomputation reproduces the committed reference bit-for-bit (energy delta 0.0, max-force delta 0.0 kJ/mol/nm); the stored Float32 config-0 force array differs from the double recomputation by at most 4.9e-4 kJ/mol/nm. The engine's Float32 numbers sit 6.4e-3 kJ/mol and 2e-4 kJ/mol/nm from the double oracle, far inside the 0.05 tolerances.

derivation.not_reproducible_part: The exact Open Force Field Toolkit version used by the source author is not recorded; the committed parameters/coordinates define this fixture, not a re-run of ligand parameterization.
derivation.reproducible_part: The derived files and every geometry/count/parameter check in tools/verify_protein_ligand.py; the parent files are pinned by SHA-256 and MIT-licensed.
steps: Load complex_plus_water.parm7 with ParmEd and complex_coords.pdb with OpenMM PDBFile.
Select all atoms whose residue name is not HOH, WAT, NA, CL, Na+ or Cl- (2615 atoms: 2601 protein + 14 UNL).
Assign the selected coordinates in prmtop atom order; remove the periodic box.
Write protein_ligand.prmtop, protein_ligand.inpcrd and a provenance PDB with the same order.

discrepancies: The earlier freeenergylab/amber_tutorials attribution was wrong; see attribution_correction.
The prmtop is a locally written ParmEd export (VERSION DATE 11/13/26 12:25:17), so its bytes are not an upstream artifact; its parameters and coordinates are derived from the pinned MIT source files.
The exact OpenFF Toolkit/force-field version is not recorded by the source; parameters are consumed as stored.

parameter_provenance.ligand_force_field: OpenForceField-parameterized catechol (residue UNL, 14 atoms); ligand atom-type labels C1/O1/H1/H2, ligand charges sum to 0.0 e
parameter_provenance.note: Neither the fixture nor the cited repository records the exact Open Force Field Toolkit / force-field version used for the ligand. The reference is defined by these committed parameters and coordinates, not by re-running a ligand parameterization.
parameter_provenance.prmtop_atom_type_note: AMBER_ATOM_TYPE strings are element-class labels (N1, H1, C1, C2, O1, O2, S1, H1..H8): 21 nonbonded type indices share 14 labels, i.e. the layout of an OpenMM System exported through ParmEd rather than a tleap-written prmtop. Ligand and protein parameters are therefore consumed as stored in this file.
parameter_provenance.protein_force_field_evidence: 159 of 162 protein residues have partial charges identical to OpenMM's amber14/protein.ff14SB.xml templates (max delta 2.2e-09 e). The three excluded residues are MET 1 and LYS 162 (terminal cap atoms H2/H3 and OXT are not in the internal templates) and HIS 30 (OpenMM names the protonation templates HID/HIE/HIP).

pdb_title: Catechol in complex with T4 lysozyme L99A/M102Q
pose_statement: This fixture is the 1XEP crystal pose of T4 lysozyme L99A/M102Q with catechol, kept in the deposited crystallographic frame (protein heavy atoms bit-identical to 1XEP chain A). The ligand is the deposited CAQ altloc A geometry within 0.014 A after atom-name mapping. It is not a generated, docked, minimized-into-place or otherwise synthetic pose, and it is not an affinity or free-energy result.
role: Static parameter/force-field fixture for the Phase-2 AMBER importer (one solute-only prmtop/inpcrd/pdb set plus one OpenMM NoCutoff reference). It is not a trajectory, not an MD result, and not a binding-affinity estimate.

source.description: MIT-licensed example: 1XEP T4 lysozyme + catechol, OpenForceField ligand parameterization, combined Amber topology exported by ParmEd.

files.role: parent solvated prmtop: 18461 atoms (protein + UNL catechol + HOH/NA/CL), triclinic 60-degree box
matching coordinate frame; atom names/order match the prmtop

evidence.check: protein heavy atoms vs 1XEP chain A (altloc ' ' or A)
evidence.result: 1290 of 1290 matched atoms are bit-identical (max deviation 0.000 A); the fixture keeps the deposited crystallographic frame with no rigid-body transform

evidence.check: catechol ligand (UNL) vs 1XEP HETATM CAQ altloc A after ring-order mapping (C1<-C6, C2<-C1, C3<-C2, C4<-C3, C5<-C4, C6<-C5, O1<-O4, O2<-O3)
evidence.result: heavy-atom RMSD 0.0075 A, max 0.0133 A (1XEP CAQ altloc B is 0.169 A away and was not used); the residual is coordinate precision, not a different conformer
162 resolved residues, MET1..LYS162 of T4 lysozyme, including the L99A/M102Q affinity-mutation sites of 1XEP (ParmEd numbers the residues 0..161, one lower than the deposited numbering)
one UNL residue, 14 atoms C6H6O2, one six-membered all-carbon ring, two C-O bonds, four aromatic C-H and two O-H; i.e. catechol (benzene-1,2-diol)

structure_provenance.statement: The coordinates are the 1XEP crystal pose, not a synthetic or hand-placed pose and not a docked pose.
